ms.report:
Hi Milestone Reviewers,

Here is the Milestone 2 PoA. I’d like to point out that some controls don’t look exactly like the mockups because I wanted to make the UI more user-friendly. For that reason, a few components have been repositioned and others now include additional icons. I also encountered limitations in VS Code and tried to adhere to its design guidelines. In particular, since VS Code restricts sidebar icon size, I replaced the original icon to make it more visible to users. The gutter panel in the ULPC tab was updated, too, so it shows exactly where you can set a breakpoint—this isn’t a classical programming language, and some details weren’t obvious before. Additionally, the budget section text now turns red when execution units are overspent.
However, the core logic and components remain unchanged; the underlying idea is exactly the same. In my view, the overall result is much better.

ms.report:
Hi Milestone Reviewers,
I have resubmitted the Milestone 3 PoA. Previously, it was rejected because the Milestone 2 PoA had not yet been signed off. Now that Milestone 2 PoA has been approved, could you please review the Milestone 3 PoA submission? Thank you.
Here is the Milestone 3 PoA. The term view has undergone a thorough reconsideration to make it more readable, informative, and concise.
The main code consists of:
 • term-viewer.ts for rendering in a VS Code tab
 • uplc.tmLanguage.json for highlighting term types, built-ins, constant types, and other constructs correctly
Where possible, terms and constants have been inlined onto a single line to improve readability.
This representation leverages VS Code features such as code folding, the minimap bar for search and navigation, and group collapsing.
I’ve also added a hint feature (press Ctrl + Alt + H to enable) that displays hints near of terms, built-in types, and constant types, I think it's very helpful for newcomers.
I hope you like the new look!
Video demo:
https://youtu.be/Y1JpHMrSxWs

ms.promise:
• Debugger engine codebase.
• Integration of the debugger engine with Aiken-UPLC.

ms.criteria:
• Debugger Engine: Should have all the features needed to support the UI based on the API definitions from Milestone 2.
• Integration: Debugger engine should be integrated with aiken-uplc to decode UPLC bytecode and to run a script.
• Communication Layer: The debugger engine, implemented in Rust, should be compiled into WebAssembly (WASM) with a JS-WASM communication layer.
• UI integration: Should work with the UI components from Milestone 2 and 3.
• Modifications: If any issues with Aiken’s UPLC module were found in Milestone 1, fix them in this milestone by creating a fork of the repository
